news_drafts.headline: Flintshire's auditors clear accounts despite social care spending pressures
news_drafts.lead: The Auditor General has given Flintshire an unqualified opinion on its 2025/26 accounts, finding no material doubts about the council's ability to continue operating. The council achieved a £0.790m underspend despite significant demand-led overspends in social care: residential care for older people ran £1.763m over budget, homecare £1.632m over, and out-of-county placements for learning disability £2.573m over. The council offset these through underspends in fleet services and regulatory services, and achieved 96% of its planned cost reductions. Council Fund reserves rose to £17.257m, above the policy minimum of £8.985m. However, the council faces continued financial pressure from Welsh Government funding that increased only 3.8% in 2025/26, below the Welsh average of 4.5%, with no revenue allocations announced for 2027/28 onwards. The council described the funding outlook as "extremely challenging" and added £1.205m from additional Welsh Government money to reserves to build resilience against future shortfalls.

news_drafts.headline: Flintshire auditor clears council accounts despite social care spending pressures
news_drafts.lead: The Auditor General has given Flintshire County Council an unqualified opinion on its 2025/26 accounts, finding no material uncertainties about the council's ability to continue operating. The council underspent its overall budget by £0.790m, but this masked significant demand-led overspends in social services: residential care for older people went over budget by £1.763m, homecare by £1.632m and out-of-county placements for learning disability services by £2.573m. The council offset these through underspends elsewhere, including a £1.300m delay in ultra-low emission vehicle (ULEV) fleet replacements and £1.036m in pay award savings, achieving 96% of budgeted cost reductions. Council Fund reserves increased to £17.257m, above the policy minimum of £8.985m, bolstered by a £1.205m contribution from Welsh Government's funding floor. However, Flintshire's funding settlement of 3.8% for 2025/26 lagged the Welsh average of 4.5%, and Welsh Government has given no indication of revenue allocations beyond 2027/28, described by the council as "extremely challenging" for financial planning.

news_drafts.headline: Flintshire borrows £25m for capital spending as rates outlook shifts
news_drafts.lead: Flintshire County Council took out £25m in borrowing (Public Works Loan Board loans, the government's lending arm for councils) during 2025/26 to fund long-term capital needs, according to its Treasury Management Annual Report reviewed by the cabinet on 15 September. Treasury advisors explored early repayment options for existing PWLB loans but rejected them as the premiums were too expensive to make refinancing worthwhile. The council maintained an average interest rate of 4.09 per cent on its investment portfolio despite Bank Rate falling during the year, reflecting disciplined cash management. The Governance and Audit Committee and Cabinet identified no significant issues with the council's treasury governance or compliance, though the outlook for interest rates has shifted from downward to uncertain due to geopolitical risk in the Middle East.

findings.headline: Income misclassification found: £426,000 coded as capital grant instead of revenue.
findings.detail: One instance identified where revenue income of £426,000 was incorrectly classified as capital grant income. Review of the entire capital grant population confirmed this was isolated. No amendment to accounts required. Auditor recommended checks of income categorisation prior to account compilation. Management accepted and committed to reminding finance officers of correct treatment by 31 March 2027.
findings.matters: Income misclassification distorts the revenue versus capital split and can mask the council's true spending and financing position. While isolated, it indicates a control weakness in income coding procedures that should be monitored.
findings.figures: £426,000 misclassified; this was the only error identified in the entire capital grant population.
findings.quote: Our audit identified one instance where revenue income of £426,000 had been incorrectly classified as capital grant income. We reviewed the capital grant population, and it was confirmed this was the only error

findings.headline: No material uncertainties identified relating to going concern.
findings.detail: The auditor has concluded that use of the going concern basis of accounting is appropriate. No material uncertainties have been identified relating to events or conditions that could cast significant doubt on the council's ability to continue as a going concern for at least 12 months from the financial statement authorisation date.
findings.matters: Going concern status underpins financial statement reliability and the council's ability to repay borrowing. Identification of material going concern issues would signal financial distress and potential covenant breach or default risk.
findings.figures: No quantitative thresholds; qualitative assessment based on audit procedures.
findings.quote: Based on the work I have performed, I have not identified any material uncertainties relating to events or conditions that, individually or collectively, may cast significant doubt on the Flintshire County Council and the group's ability to continue to adopt the going concern basis of accounting

findings.headline: Unqualified audit opinion issued on 2025-26 accounts with no uncorrected misstatements.
findings.detail: An unqualified audit opinion will be issued confirming the financial statements give a true and fair view of the council's financial position as at 31 March 2026 and have been properly prepared. No uncorrected misstatements were identified. One corrected misstatement involved reclassification of Property, Plant and Equipment items between asset categories with no net impact on the summary statements.
findings.matters: An unqualified opinion confirms the reliability of the council's published financial statements used by lenders in creditworthiness assessment. Absence of uncorrected misstatements ensures the financial position is fairly stated.
findings.figures: One corrected reclassification: Other land and Buildings £16.317m to £5.578m; Assets Under Construction £1.063m to £11.802m; no net impact on accounts.
findings.quote: We intend to issue an unqualified opinion on the accounts

findings.headline: Mutual Investment Model project for school construction properly accounted for with no audit issues.
findings.detail: The council has entered a Mutual Investment Model project for construction of a new primary and secondary school with associated infrastructure and maintenance. The auditor reviewed the full MIM contract, assessed asset recognition on the balance sheet, evaluated assumptions in valuing the asset and forecasting unitary charges, and verified disclosures of long-term commitments and financial obligations. No issues identified.
findings.matters: MIM arrangements create long-term financial obligations materially affecting cash flows and the council's future debt servicing capacity. Proper accounting and full disclosure of these commitments is essential for lenders assessing repayment ability.
findings.figures: No specific financial figures for the MIM project provided in this report.
findings.quote: The Council has entered a MIM project for the construction of a new primary and secondary school and associated infrastructure and maintenance.

findings.headline: Triennial pension fund revaluation implemented for first time in 2025-26 accounts.
findings.detail: A triennial valuation of the Local Government Pension Scheme was undertaken as at 31 March 2025 and will impact disclosures in the council's 2025-26 financial statements for the first time. The audit team assessed the actuary's competence, tested data accuracy, and reviewed the reasonableness of assumptions. No issues were identified with the valuation.
findings.matters: Pension liabilities are material to the council's balance sheet. A triennial revaluation represents a material change to liability measurement that affects the reported financial position and covenant compliance ratios lenders monitor.
findings.figures: Triennial valuation dated 31 March 2025; specific pension liability quantum not disclosed in this report.
findings.quote: A triennial valuation of the scheme has been undertaken as at 31 March 2025, which will impact upon disclosures in the Council's financial statements for the first time in the 2025-26 financial year.
